mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) directly compresses the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, with the effect being proportional to the level of the rate (lower rates predict higher returns).
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 12 months is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes corporate earnings contraction and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.5% (or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decreases in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate a tightening monetary cycle amid a strong labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to rising real rates and reduced corporate profit margins.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls (or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1300 and a negative growth rate in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals a weakening consumer demand cycle, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances meeting the trigger condition (HOUST < 1300 and RSAFS growth negative) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong labor market conditions, as measured by high employment growth (PAYEMS), directly support corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, with the effect being proportional to the level of employment.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS is above 145000 (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.05 over 12 months.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 240 indicates elevated inflation pressures, which typically triggers a hawkish monetary policy response and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to rising real interest rates and reduced equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 240 (or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) coupled with a rise in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a shift from housing-driven to manufacturing-driven economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as the market prices in resilient industrial output.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST falls and INDPRO rises (or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained slowdown in industrial production (INDPRO) growth below 0.5% for three consecutive months signals a supply-side shock, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate output and potential inflationary pressures.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO growth is below 0.5% for 3 months (or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window).
